subject: science
intro: I'm Mr. Patel. Let's plan a 6th grade lesson where students gather evidence that living things are made of cells.

beats.narration: Starting from the question "is it alive?" makes cells the evidence, not just vocabulary.
beats.text: Is It Alive? Looking for Cells

beats.narration: This standard asks students to investigate and provide evidence that living things are made of cells.
"Cite evidence" keeps it a science practice lesson, not a labeling lesson.
beats.text: Students will be able to use a microscope to observe cells in different samples and cite evidence that living things are made of cells.

beats.narration: The cork is a great discussion piece, since it was once alive.
beats.text: Mystery samples: a cork, an onion, a rock, and a leaf. Students predict which are or were alive and explain how they could tell.

beats.narration: Rushing the technique leads to frustration, so I model it carefully.
beats.text: Model microscope technique: preparing a wet mount, focusing from low to high power, and sketching accurately. Show Hooke's cork drawing for historical context.

beats.narration: Including sand gives them a non-living comparison.
beats.text: Stations: students view onion skin, cheek cells (prepared slides), elodea leaf, and sand. They sketch each and record "cells: yes/no."

beats.narration: Their own sketches become the evidence in their answer.
beats.text: Which samples had cells? Use your sketches as evidence to explain whether all living things are made of cells.

outro: Predict, model technique, observe, argue from evidence. Your turn.
